$comment: Read ONLY by scripts/test/ci-lane-closure-test.mjs, never by the merge-gate selector: what a lane watches is still stated once, in its own `on: push: paths:`.
sources: test files a lane's runner collects without any command naming them (Vitest, `go test ./...`), scanned for `../` reads.
declared: reads no text scan can resolve (a Gradle system property, a template literal, `$script_name`). Each must exist and select its lane.
knownGaps: real reads a lane's filter deliberately does not watch. `coveredBy` names a lane that runs the same code on that change and is verified; a gap without it is an open decision, not a pass.

sourceJobs / sources[].jobs: which of a lane's jobs execute a source (web: light jobs vs SERVER_JOBS of scripts/ci/web-lane-scope.mjs). ignoredReads: scanned reads that are not reads (with the reason); each must still be produced by the scan or it is stale.

knownGaps.why: android.yml's `:protocol:test` opens the shared fixtures, and so does compat.yml's android-protocol job — unfiltered, on every pull request, required by the merge gate. android.yml deliberately names no apps/RelayiumKit path (its header; scripts/test/swift-ci-boundary-test.mjs PARSED). The Gradle half of W-N18 still matters there and is enforced separately below.

apps/windows/test/unit reads crypto, realtime-wire and store-wire vectors. Each is held byte-equal to its generator under web/scripts by check-wire-vectors.mjs in the unfiltered compat.yml, so a fixture-only edit fails compat, and a legitimate one changes a web/scripts generator — which windows.yml watches. windows.yml deliberately names no apps/RelayiumKit path (its header).

contracts.yml's web-contract job runs one Vitest file from web/src; the same file runs in web.yml's `npm test`, which every web/src change selects. contracts.yml watches only the contract document on purpose (scripts/test/fixtures/ci-path-selection.mjs, contracts row).
contracts.yml's go-contract job pins its toolchain with server/go.mod and runs a `go test` that go.yml's `go test ./...` also runs on any server change.
ops-deploy-contract.yml's Go consumer lives in server/ and runs inside go.yml's `go test ./...` (ci-path-selection.mjs, ops-deploy-v1 row).
swift-package.yml sets up Go only for the Swift<->Go interop classes it runs forced; inbox-swift-interop.yml runs exactly those classes, with a named-execution proof, on every server change.

OPEN: ios.yml's ios-transfer-acceptance builds and runs the whole Go server (scripts/lib/local-acceptance.sh acceptance_build), but PATH_MATRIX row 1 deliberately keeps the 75-minute iOS lane off server-only changes. No other lane runs the iOS built-App acceptance. Revisit: owner accepts iOS runs on server changes, or the acceptance moves to a lane that watches server/**.

OPEN: apps/mac/scripts/test-release-readiness.sh checks that server/account/{auth.go,handlers.go,devices_bearer_test.go} EXIST (evidence list, not content). handlers.go alone had 33 commits in 60 days; watching it would start the paid macOS lane (UI smoke + signed build) on each. A rename/delete fails macos on its next run instead. Revisit: owner accepts the cost, or the evidence check moves to a lane that watches server/**.

web.why: skipped in the `test` job (RELAYIUM_GO_INTEROP=0); only `npm run test:interop` in sealed-box-interop runs it

ignoredReads.why: `join(webRoot, "../server/account")` where webRoot is a temporary fixture directory; the test writes its own catalog there and never opens the repository's server/account
